pages.text: Nigerians among 12 suspects arrested in Canada luxury car theft syndicate Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Nigerians among 12 suspects arrested in $4.5m Canada luxury car theft syndicate 8 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Basillioh Rukanga Peel Regional Police Canadian authorities say organised vehicle theft is a serious crime threatening the security of communities Canadian police have arrested 12 suspects, including eight Nigerians, in an investigation into an alleged car theft syndicate. They are accused of stealing luxury vehicles and shipping them to West Africa. Police in the Peel region of Ontario said they had recovered 96 high-value vehicles concealed in shipping containers. The vehicles, valued at $4.5m (£3.4m) were destined for export via Canadian ports. The trafficking of vehicles from North America and Europe to African countries has been a long-standing concern for law enforcement agencies. The suspects face 231 charges, with arrest warrants issued for others. Police say some of the accused may face deportation after their criminal proceedings are concluded. The arrests followed months of what police described as an "extensive auto theft investigation". The investigations began in March in partnership with Canada's border agency after police identified a warehouse allegedly being used to store stolen vehicles. pages.description: In 75 years, the United Nations, its specialised agencies, related agencies, funds, programmes and staff were awarded the prestigious Nobel Peace Prize twelve times.
pages.text: Nobel Peace Prize AR | الأمم المتحدة Skip to main content الأمم المتحدة وجائزة نوبل للسلام الأمم المتحدة وجائزة نوبل للسلام استلهم ألفريد نوبل وصيته التي حررها عام 1895 من إيمانه بوحدة الأسرة الإنسانية. ونصّت الوصية على أن تُمنح جائزة نوبل للسلام للشخص الذي يبذل أكبر جهد في سبيل «تعزيز الأخوّة بين الأمم، وإلغاء الجيوش الدائمة أو تقليصها، وعقد مؤتمرات السلام وتشجيعها». مُنحت جائزة نوبل للسلام المرموقة 13 مرة للأمم المتحدة و وكالاتها المتخصصة وصناديقها وبرامجها ، والمنظمات المرتبطة بها، ولمسؤولين حاليين وسابقين في المنظمة. وقد نالت المفوضية السامية للأمم المتحدة لشؤون اللاجئين هذه الجائزة مرتين، في عامي 1954 و 1981 . وكرّمت لجنة نوبل النرويجية أيضًا أمينين عامين للأمم المتحدة، هما كوفي عنان و داغ همرشولد ، تقديرًا لجهودهما. وعقب فوزه بالجائزة مناصفة مع الأمم المتحدة عام 2001، أعرب الأمين العام كوفي عنان، في كلمة وجهها إلى موظفي المنظمة، عن أمله في أن «تدفعنا هذه الجائزة إلى المضي قدمًا، وتشجعنا جميعًا على النهوض بمهامنا بعزيمة أشد». «على مدى مئة عام، سعت لجنة نوبل النرويجية إلى توطيد التعاون المنظّم بين الدول. وقد أتاحت نهاية الحرب الباردة للأمم المتحدة أخيرًا أن تنهض على نحو أكمل بالدور الذي أُنشئت من أجله. وتقف المنظمة اليوم في طليعة الجهود الرامية إلى تحقيق السلام والأمن في العالم، وفي صدارة التعبئة الدولية لمواجهة التحديات الاقتصادية والاجتماعية والبيئية التي تواجه العالم... وتود لجنة نوبل النرويجية، في عامها المئوي، أن تعلن أن الطريق الوحيد القائم على التفاوض لتحقيق السلام والتعاون على الصعيد العالمي يمر عبر الأمم المتحدة». معهد نوبل النرويجي أوسلو، 12 تشرين الأول/أكتوبر 2001 الحائزون على جائزة نوبل من الأمم المتحدة 2026 - نافانيثيم بيلاي مُنحت جائزة نوبل للسلام لعام 202

pages.text: Norfolk holidaymaker says visa error blocked entry to Italy Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Holidaymaker says visa error blocked entry to Italy 1 hour ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Owen Sennitt Norfolk Paula Pugh Paula Pugh, pictured with her husband Andy, was refused entry into Italy A holidaymaker said she believed she was refused entry at the Italian border due to a computer error that recorded her as having overstayed a visa. Paula Pugh, 61, from Swaffham, Norfolk, travelled from Stansted Airport to Calabria in southern Italy for a five-day holiday to celebrate her husband's birthday in September. After arriving she was told she had exceeded her 90-day visa-free allowance to the Schengen area and was put on a return flight, but Pugh said this was a database error and that she had only spent 22 days in the area. The European Commission said it is the responsibility of individual countries to correct any errors. The 61-year-old said the experience made her feel "like a criminal", but so far she has been unable to identify the source of the error. Her experience also cost her hundreds of pounds after she had to pay for her return flight back to the UK and she lost money she had already spent on the holiday. Pugh and her husband arrived at Reggio Calabria Airport at 12:40 BST but was denied entry. pages.text: North Dakota Badlands 2026: When to visit, where to stay, and what to do | National Geographic TRAVEL BEST OF THE WORLD Why you should visit the rugged North Dakota Badlands in 2026 Discover the best seasons to visit, where to stay near Theodore Roosevelt National Park, and how to explore this otherworldly landscape. The Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library is set to open in July 2026 outside Medora, North Dakota. Photograph by Image Professionals GmbH, Alamy Stock Photo By Stephanie Pearson Published October 21, 2025 Theodore Roosevelt first traveled to the Badlands on a hunting trip in 1883. He was so taken by the otherworldly landscape of pastel buttes, trilling meadowlarks, and disappearing bison, that he returned in 1884 to grieve the simultaneous deaths of his wife and mother, raising cattle and working on the wild frontier for almost three years. Its “desolate, grim beauty” so changed Roosevelt that he famously wrote, “I would not have been president had it not been for my experience in North Dakota .” Opening on July 4, 2026, the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library celebrates the Badlands as much as it does the 26th president. Designed by Norwegian architectural firm Snøhetta, the state-of-the-art, sustainable library sits high on a lonely butte outside of Medora, a military camp turned frontier town named after a French nobleman’s wife. The 93,000-square-foot library disappears into its surroundings, camouflaged by a living roof sprouting native plants, part of a 1.3-mile walking trail that provides sweeping views toward the national park. Sir Mark Rowley, Britain's most senior police officer, recently said policing was "heading for failure" without change and has proposed between eight and 10 regional forces should be established. But Jo Coles, York and North Yorkshire's Labour deputy mayor, warned bigger forces would jeopardise links between officers and their communities, adding that merging forces would prove a "distraction" and would "take resources from the front line". A Home Office spokesperson said the current model of policing "has not changed since the 1960s and is no longer fit for purpose". Coles, whose role is to oversee both North Yorkshire Police and North Yorkshire Fire and Rescue Service, said she and York and North Yorkshire's elected mayor David Skaith were, however, not opposed to the creation of a National Police Service to tackle serious cross-border crime. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Northern California District Office The BLM’s Northern California District manages about 3.5 million acres of public lands, covering a diverse landscape, ranging from the arid and rugged Great Basin to the fog shrouded forests of the North Coast. The Redding-based district office oversees field offices in Alturas, Arcata, Redding and Susanville and a field station in Cedarville. The district contains two distinct regions. On the east, the Applegate and Eagle Lake field offices oversee vast expanses of public lands in a high desert landscape, including about a million and a half acres in far western Nevada. Small communities depend on public lands for economic benefits, primarily through livestock grazing, and tourism uses ranging from hunting to mountain biking. These lands provide habitat for 14 wild horse herds and special status species, such as greater sage grouse. On the west, the Arcata and Redding field offices manage smaller, scattered blocks of public land with more emphasis on recreation demands from urban areas. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Northwest District Office The Northwest Colorado District manages about 3.15 million surface acres and is comprised of the Kremmling, Little Snake and White River field offices. The district includes the upper Colorado River corridor along with the White and Yampa rivers. It is home to some of the largest deer and elk herds in the area, along with pronghorn, bighorn sheep and a wide variety of other wildlife. The Northwest District contains the majority of the Colorado range of the Greater Sage Grouse. The Northwest District also manages 7.1 million acres of subsurface minerals, which includes some of the most productive oil and natural gas fields in the state, four of Colorado’s nine coal mines and vast deposits of oil shale. pages.text: Nvidia: How the Jensen Huang scandal exposed a headache for business-friendly Singapore Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live How the Jensen Huang scandal created a headache for business-friendly Singapore 3 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Tessa Wong and Osmond Chia , Singapore Getty Images A major scandal involving Nvidia founder Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy based in Singapore has cast a spotlight on the city-state's success as a global chip hub - and a location for alleged illicit trade. On Thursday, Huang stepped down from the US chip giant after admitting he had an affair. He was reportedly involved with a woman named Alice Huang, who ran Singaporean data centre company Megaspeed, a major buyer of Nvidia's chips. pages.text: Oficina de Normas de Gestión Laboral | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Oficina de Normas de Gestión Laboral La Oficina de Normas de Gestión Laboral (Office of Labor-Management Standards, u OLMS, por sus siglas en inglés) pertenece al Departamento de Trabajo de los Estados Unidos y es responsable de administrar y aplicar la mayoría de las disposiciones de la Ley de Notificación y Divulgación Gestión Laboral (Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act, o LMRDA, por sus siglas en inglés). Dicha ley fue adoptada con el fin de garantizar normas básicas de democracia y responsabilidad fiscal en las organizaciones laborales del sector privado. Los sindicatos que representan a los empleados del Correo Postal de los Estados Unidos también se hallan sujetos a la LMRDA. Los sindicatos de empleados federales se hallan sujetos a normas similares conforme a la Ley de Reforma del Servicio Civil de 1978 (Civil Service Reform Act, o CSRA, por sus siglas in inglés) y a la Ley del Servicio Exterior de 1980. La OLMS anima a que los oficiales y los miembros del sindicato, así como otros individuos afectados por la LMRDA, se pongan en contacto con la agencia para discutir de problemas, presenten quejas u obtengan información sobre la LMRDA. Además, la OLMS fomenta la conformidad voluntaria con la LMRDA al informar a oficiales del sindicato y a otros individuos de sus responsabilidades y al animar a los miembros del sindicato a que ejerzan sus derechos. It allows different vendors to work together, encouraging competition, driving new ideas, and creating smarter, more efficient networks. Open RAN is a step toward more reliable wireless communications. Next generation RANs are characterized by the disaggregation of the network elements and the use of intelligent controllers to manage the increased complexity of radio technologies and network deployments. The disaggregation of the network elements to create an Open RAN that allows the equipment from different vendors to communicate requires well-defined, standardized interfaces. Furthermore, the increased complexity of the network and the need for real-time control forces the network operators to investigate automated solutions based on Machine Learning (ML) algorithms. The most well-known opinions are those released or announced in cases in which the Court has heard oral argument. Each opinion sets out the Court’s judgment and its reasoning and may include the majority or principal opinion as well as any concurring or dissenting opinions. All opinions in a single case are published together and are prefaced by a syllabus prepared by the Reporter of Decisions that summarizes the Court’s decision. The Justice who authors the majority or principal opinion often will summarize the opinion from the bench during a Court session. The Court may also dispose of cases in per curiam opinions, which do not identify the author. These cases frequently resolve cases summarily, often without oral argument. But per curiam opinions have sometimes been issued in argued cases. Try again ADVANCED SEARCH DOCKET SEARCH Search Home > Oral Arguments Argument Transcripts Argument Audio Calendars and Lists Courtroom Seating Oral Arguments The Court holds oral argument in about 70-80 cases each year. The arguments are an opportunity for the Justices to ask questions directly of the attorneys representing the parties to the case, and for the attorneys to highlight arguments that they view as particularly important. Arguments are generally scheduled on specified Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday mornings beginning on the first Monday in October, and continuing through the end of April. Typically, the Court holds two arguments each day beginning at 10:00 a.m. The days on which arguments are held are identified on the Court’s yearly calendar . The specific cases to be argued each day, and the attorneys scheduled to argue them, are identified on hearing lists for each session and on the day call for each argument session. The Court is currently conducting a pilot program in which members of the public may apply for Courtroom seating through an online lottery . During this pilot program, Courtroom seating will also be available to the public on a first-come, first-seated basis. An audio feed of the argument is live-streamed on the Court's website, and the Court posts the audio later in the day. pages.description: The goal of the CORE Network is to build upon the best of what we currently do across FDA in incident response, and not only to streamline, but to strengthen FDA's efforts to prevent, detect, investigate, respond to, and learn from incidents and outbreaks.
pages.text: Outbreaks of Foodborne Illness | FDA Skip to main content Skip to FDA Search Skip to in this section menu Skip to footer links Home Food Recalls, Outbreaks & Emergencies Outbreaks of Foodborne Illness Recalls, Outbreaks & Emergencies In this section When two or more people get the same illness from the same contaminated food or drink, the event is called a foodborne illness outbreak . FDA investigates outbreaks to control them, so more people do not get sick in the outbreak, and to learn how to prevent similar outbreaks from happening in the future. FDA’s Coordinated Outbreak Response and Evaluation (CORE) Network was created to manage not just outbreak response, but surveillance and post-response activities related to incidents involving multiple illnesses linked to FDA-regulated human food, dietary supplements, and cosmetic products. Learn how outbreaks are investigated . Note: Not all recalls, alerts, and advisories result in an outbreak of foodborne illness. Check recent Food Recalls and Safety Alerts . Investigations Outbreak Investigations are managed by FDA’s CORE Response Teams . The investigations are in a variety of stages, meaning that some outbreaks have limited information, and others may be near completion. Advisories Public health advisories are issued for outbreak investigations that have resulted in specific, actionable steps for consumers to take to protect themselves. ENSURING UNION DEMOCRACY UNION OFFICER ELECTIONS OLMS investigates union members' complaints concerning union officer elections and seeks to set aside and rerun those few elections in which it finds a violation that may have affected the results. Please view the union election decisions page for further information. UNION TRUSTEESHIPS OLMS investigates complaints concerning union trusteeships. Please view the trusteeship decisions page for more information. MONITORING UNION ASSETS COMPLIANCE AUDITS & INVESTIGATIONS OLMS audits and investigates unions to ensure their compliance with the LMRDA and to protect unions from becoming victims of embezzlements.
